**TASK 1 – SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION**

**Proposed System Title:** Water Refilling Station Delivery System

**Organization or Intended Environment:** Water refilling station businesses that offer water gallon delivery services to customers.

**System Description:** The system will manage customer information, water orders, delivery schedules, riders, payments, and container deposits. It will help the business monitor deliveries and unpaid customer balances.

**Existing Process:** The business currently records customer orders, deliveries, and payments manually using notebooks, paper receipts, or messaging applications.

**Problems Encountered:**

- Difficulty tracking customer deliveries and order status.
- Unpaid balances are not properly monitored.
- Customer and payment records can be lost or misplaced.
- Delivery schedules and rider assignments are difficult to organize.

**Why the System Is Necessary:** The system is necessary to make order management, delivery tracking, and payment monitoring faster, easier, and more organized.

**TASK 2 – PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION**

| **Problem**                            | **What Is Happening**                                                          | **Who Is Affected**                 | **Consequences**                                                              | **Proposed Solution**                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Manual Delivery Tracking               | Deliveries and their statuses are recorded manually.                           | Owner, staff, and riders            | Difficulty monitoring pending, ongoing, and completed deliveries.             | Provide delivery status tracking and rider assignment.                  |
| Unpaid Customer Balances               | Payments and remaining balances are not consistently monitored.                | Owner and staff                     | Missed payments and inaccurate payment histories.                             | Record full and partial payments and calculate outstanding balances.    |
| Disorganized Orders and Gallon Records | Orders, available gallons, returns, and deposits are kept in separate records. | Owner, staff, riders, and customers | Lost orders, recording errors, and inaccurate inventory or container records. | Provide centralized order, inventory, and container deposit management. |

**TASK 3 – PROJECT OBJECTIVES**

**General Objective**

To develop a Water Refilling Station Delivery System that improves the management of customer orders, delivery operations, gallon inventory, and payment records, particularly outstanding customer balances.

Specific Objectives:

To develop a system that records customer information and water delivery orders.

To provide delivery status tracking and rider assignment for monitoring pending and completed deliveries.

To maintain payment records and identify customers with unpaid or partially paid balances.

To manage gallon inventory and container deposits to improve the monitoring of available gallons and reusable containers.

**TASK 4 – TARGET USERS**

| **User Type**         | **Primary Responsibilities**                                                                                          | **Access Level / Permissions**                                                                 |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Administrator / Owner | Manage user accounts, customer records, orders, inventory, riders, payments, deposits, routes, and reports.           | Full access to system administration and station records.                                      |
| Regular User / Staff  | Register customers, record and update orders, record payments, and monitor outstanding balances.                      | Add, view, and update records according to assigned permissions.                               |
| Delivery Rider        | View assigned deliveries, check customer addresses, update delivery status, and report delivered or returned gallons. | View assigned deliveries and update delivery status; no access to unrelated sensitive records. |

**TASK 5 – INITIAL DATABASE PLANNING**

The following eight initial database entities support the features described in Chapter I.

| **Entity Name**   | **Business Purpose**                                                              | **Information to Be Stored (Key Attributes)**                                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Customer          | Stores customer information.                                                      | Customer_ID (PK), Name, Address, Contact_Number                                               |
| Order             | Records customer water orders.                                                    | Order_ID (PK), Customer_ID (FK), Order_Date, Quantity, Total_Amount, Order_Status             |
| Gallon            | Stores water gallon and product information.                                      | Gallon_ID (PK), Gallon_Type, Price, Stock_Quantity                                            |
| Delivery          | Records and monitors customer deliveries.                                         | Delivery_ID (PK), Order_ID (FK), Rider_ID (FK), Route_ID (FK), Delivery_Date, Delivery_Status |
| Rider             | Stores delivery rider information.                                                | Rider_ID (PK), Name, Contact_Number                                                           |
| Payment           | Records customer payments and supports balance monitoring.                        | Payment_ID (PK), Order_ID (FK), Amount_Paid, Payment_Date, Payment_Status                     |
| Route             | Stores delivery route information.                                                | Route_ID (PK), Route_Name, Destination, Description                                           |
| Container Deposit | Records customer gallon container deposits and outstanding container obligations. | Deposit_ID (PK), Customer_ID (FK), Quantity, Deposit_Amount, Deposit_Status                   |

**TASK 6 – DBMS SELECTION**

**Database Name & Classification:** MySQL – Relational Database Management System (SQL).

**Justification**

MySQL is suitable for the Water Refilling Station Delivery System because it can organize and manage related information such as customers, orders, deliveries, riders, payments, gallon inventory, routes, and container deposits. It supports relationships between tables, making it easier to retrieve, update, and maintain records.

**Advantages**

- Free and open-source.
- Suitable for organizing related data in tables.
- Supports relationships between tables.
- Provides accesscontrol and database security features when configured properly.
- Can handle growing amounts of structured business data.

**Limitations**

- Requires proper database configuration.
- Needs regular backups and maintenance.
- Requires basic SQL knowledge.
- Database security depends on correct configuration, permissions, and responsible administration.

**Management & Modeling Tools**

- MySQL – For storing and managing database records.
- phpMyAdmin – For managing the MySQL database through a web browser.
- MySQL Workbench – For designing and managing database structures.
